name: MiBeta (187Re)
summary: MiBeta was a historical direct neutrino-mass experiment using silver-perrhenate microcalorimeters. It studied the low-energy beta spectrum of rhenium-187 with the source embedded in the detector.
detection_principle: Low-temperature AgReO4 absorbers measure the decay energy as a thermal pulse. Only the antineutrino escapes, so the shape near the beta endpoint carries the effective mass information.

status.label: Completed / historical

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
